objective: 0.3.0 pi 1/10: Add the packages/integrations/pi package that generates a Pi package from the shared runtime instructions, so the Pi integration has a scaffold, a build and a sync check beside the Claude plugin.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim): "please add intents for the next 0.3.0 release where I will implement the pi extension integration"; the maintainer implements 0.3.0, so these Intents record the work and carry no Assignments until the maintainer starts it.

Maintainer, 2026-11-07: implement 0.3.0 now, every part except the dropped auto-mode gate (pi 8/10); test with unit tests and recorded or synthesized fixtures only, no live Kimi runs; merge each PR once it is reviewed and green.
Maintainer (verbatim): "in the docs/pi/ it's supposed to use already existent extensions for required functionality" and "the first provider to implement will be kimi for coding global".

Release model: work lands on release/0.3.0/integration cut from main, as one release/0.3.0/<type>/<change> branch and one PR per change; the first PR of the release carries the version bump made with mise run bump:minor.
Done means mise run verify passes with the generated output in sync (mise run build) and CI green on every required check, including the windows job.
A new folder packages/integrations/pi/ sits beside packages/integrations/claude/ and reuses the runtime's domain, state, CLI and instructions without copying them.
The output is a Pi package: conventional extensions/, skills/ and prompts/ directories or a pi key in package.json, with the pi-package keyword.

The host modules @earendil-works/pi-ai, pi-agent-core, pi-coding-agent, pi-tui and typebox are peerDependencies and are not bundled. Open: the docs require the range "*" for these, while scripts/dependency-ranges.test.ts accepts only caret ranges in every dependency field; which one yields.

A second generator reads the same instruction sources as the Claude build and writes the Pi package; its paths join the generated-path list so the existing byte-for-byte sync check covers them, every generated file carries a note naming its source, and the version is synced from the root package.json by mise run build.
A sync test for the Pi output exists, modelled on packages/integrations/claude/tests/plugin.test.ts.
Every tracked path in the new package stays within the 120-character limit enforced by scripts/repo-paths.test.ts.
Decided: pi 1.5.0 is the pinned version (released 2026-11-02); pi and every reused extension are pinned and move only through mise run deps:update, which re-records the CI fixtures.
Decided (maintainer: "built js, use bun build"): the extension ships as JavaScript bundled with bun build into the generated package, guarded by the sync check.
Decided: users install with pi install git:github.com/davidbasilefilho/holyagent#holyagent-<version>, from the release tags; no npm publishing.
Decided: host modules are peerDependencies with range "*" as pi 1.5.0's package docs require; scripts/dependency-ranges.test.ts gains that exception for pi peer dependencies.
